title: Apocalypse of Abraham — Hobah Translation
about: A Jewish apocalypse preserved completely in Old Church Slavonic. Its first part tells how Abraham rejected idolatry; its second part describes his heavenly ascent, a vision of creation and history, and judgment.

translation.base_text: Old Church Slavonic textual tradition represented in the public-domain edition and English philological work of G. H. Box and J. I. Landsman (1918), with the Slavonic witness treated as the surviving base language
translation.method: Fresh modern-English rendering of the surviving Slavonic sense, using the public-domain philological edition as a control. No modern copyrighted English translation is copied.
translation.confidence: Medium; the work survives through Slavonic transmission from a lost Greek form, and some passages are corrupt or secondary
translation.notes: The translation preserves the book's received Slavonic form rather than pretending to recover the lost Greek or a hypothetical Hebrew original. Difficult names and liturgical phrases are transliterated conservatively.
translation.license_note: Ancient text and 1918 source edition are public domain. Hobah English wording is newly prepared for this project.

chapters.label: Chapter 1
chapters.text: The book of the revelation of Abraham, son of Terah, son of Nahor, son of Serug, son of Reu, son of Peleg, son of Eber, son of Shelah, son of Arpachshad, son of Shem, son of Noah. I, Abraham, was serving the gods of my father Terah and of Nahor my brother, gods made of wood and stone, gold and silver, bronze and iron. While I was trying to learn who the true mighty God is, I entered the temple of my father's idols and found the stone god Merumath fallen face-down before the iron god Nakhon. I was troubled, for though Merumath was heavy I lifted him and set him again in his place.

chapters.label: Chapter 2
chapters.text: The next day I returned and found Merumath fallen again. I could not understand how a god who could not stand by himself could help anyone. I reported it to my father. He became angry and ordered me to make another image in his workshop. As I worked, I began to reason: these things are shaped by human hands, cut and hammered and polished. How then can the work be greater than the worker?

chapters.label: Chapter 3
chapters.text: My father sent me to sell wooden idols. On the road one of them fell and broke. I gathered the pieces and carried the remaining gods to merchants from Syria. When they asked the price, I gave them what they wanted and threw the broken one into the river. I thought, ‘If it truly were a god, it would have saved itself and would not have needed me.’

chapters.label: Chapter 4
chapters.text: Returning home, I told my father that one of his gods had fallen and been destroyed. He answered that I was careless. But I said in my heart, ‘How can he call them gods when he himself repairs them?’ I took another wooden idol, Barisat, and placed it by the fire. I ordered it to watch the food while I went outside.

chapters.label: Chapter 5
chapters.text: When I returned, Barisat had fallen into the fire and was burning. I pulled it out, but its head was scorched away. I said, ‘Barisat, where is your power? You could not even save your own head.’ I laughed at the helpless image, yet my heart grieved because my father trusted in such things.

chapters.label: Chapter 6
chapters.text: I considered the elements. Fire burns wood, so perhaps fire is greater; yet water extinguishes fire. Water seems greater, but the earth drinks water. The earth seems greater, yet the sun dries the earth. The sun is mighty, but clouds hide it, and wind drives the clouds. Wind is strong, but human beings can resist it behind walls. None of these can be the God who rules all.

chapters.label: Chapter 7
chapters.text: Then I looked at the heavens, the sun, moon, and stars, each keeping its appointed course. I understood that the one who orders them must be greater than all of them. I said, ‘I seek the God who made heaven and earth, the sea and all that is in them, the one whom none of these created things can master.’

chapters.label: Chapter 8
chapters.text: While I was still speaking, a voice of the Mighty One came from heaven: ‘Abraham, Abraham!’ I answered, ‘Here I am.’ He said, ‘You are seeking the God of gods, the Creator, in the understanding of your heart. I am he. Go out from Terah your father and from his house, so that you are not destroyed in the sins of his house.’

chapters.label: Chapter 9
chapters.text: I went out. As soon as I had left, fire came down from heaven and burned my father's house and everything in it. Then the voice said to me, ‘Abraham!’ I answered, ‘Here I am.’ He said, ‘Prepare for me a sacrifice: a young heifer, a she-goat, a ram, a turtledove, and a pigeon. Go to the high mountain, and there I will show you the ages prepared by my word.’

chapters.label: Chapter 10
chapters.text: I fasted for forty days and nights and took no bread or water. On the fortieth day I saw a man coming toward me. His body was like sapphire, his face like chrysolite, the hair of his head like snow, and a turban like a rainbow upon him. His clothing was purple, and a golden staff was in his right hand. I fell on my face in fear.

chapters.label: Chapter 11
chapters.text: He said, ‘Abraham, stand up. I am Yahoel, appointed by the Eternal One. I have been sent to strengthen you and to silence the one who opposes you. Rise and go with me.’ He taught me a hymn of praise to the Eternal, the One whose name cannot be spoken by flesh, and he told me not to fear the powers we would meet.

chapters.label: Chapter 12
chapters.text: We went together toward Horeb, the mountain of God. The angel told me how to prepare the sacrifice and divide the animals, but not the birds. I did as he commanded. Birds of prey descended upon the carcasses, and I tried to drive them away.

chapters.label: Chapter 13
chapters.text: Then an unclean bird spoke to me with a human voice: ‘Abraham, what are you doing on these holy heights where no one eats or drinks? Leave the man who is with you and come with me, for you will be destroyed if you ascend.’ I asked the angel what this was. He said, ‘This is Azazel, the disgraceful one.’

chapters.label: Chapter 14
chapters.text: Yahoel said to Azazel, ‘Shame on you! Abraham's portion is in heaven, but yours is upon the earth. The Eternal has given you the dwelling of uncleanness. Through you wrath and trials come upon the generations of the wicked. Depart from this man whom God has chosen.’ He told me to say to Azazel, ‘May you be the burning coal of the furnace of the earth. Go away from me.’

chapters.label: Chapter 15
chapters.text: The sun went down. Smoke like that of a furnace rose from the sacrifice, and the angel took me by the right hand. We rose upon the wings of the pigeons that had been offered. A wind carried us upward, and I saw beneath me the earth and waters, and above us a mighty light that no human tongue can describe.

chapters.label: Chapter 16
chapters.text: I heard the sound of many waters and a roaring like the sea. I wanted to fall down, but there was no ground beneath my feet. Yahoel held me and said, ‘Remain with me. Do not be afraid.’ We passed through a fiery place where living creatures praised the Eternal One without ceasing.

chapters.label: Chapter 17
chapters.text: The angel taught me to praise: ‘Eternal, Mighty One, Holy El, self-originated, incorruptible, spotless, unborn, the one whose word created all things! Receive my prayer and the sacrifice you yourself commanded.’ As I spoke, the fire around us opened.

chapters.label: Chapter 18
chapters.text: I saw a throne of fire, and around it many-eyed living creatures. Beneath the throne were fiery wheels. The living creatures had four faces, and their wings were full of eyes. When the throne moved, the wheels moved with it, and all the host cried out in praise.

chapters.label: Chapter 19
chapters.text: A voice came from the midst of the fire: ‘Abraham!’ I answered, ‘Here I am, your servant.’ The voice said, ‘Look upon the expanses beneath your feet and understand the things I reveal to you.’ I looked down and saw many heavens, the stars and the powers set over them, and the earth beneath.

chapters.label: Chapter 20
chapters.text: I saw the earth with its regions, peoples, creatures, seas, rivers, and the abyss. I saw the garden of Eden and its fruits, and within it human beings. I also saw the place of torment, and the one who deceives, with his dominion.

chapters.label: Chapter 21
chapters.text: I asked, ‘Eternal Mighty One, what is this picture of creation that I see?’ He answered that it was the design established by his will before the things themselves came to be. What exists in the world has its appointed form and time before him.

chapters.label: Chapter 22
chapters.text: I saw on one side a multitude of people: men, women, and children. Some stood on the right side of the picture and others on the left. I asked who they were. He said, ‘Those on the right are the people set apart for me from the nations; those on the left are those who follow the path of lawlessness.’

chapters.label: Chapter 23
chapters.text: I saw Adam, a great figure, and beside him Eve. Behind a tree stood one who looked like a serpent in form, yet had hands and feet like a man. He gave them fruit from the tree. I understood that this was Azazel and that through him transgression entered the human race.

chapters.label: Chapter 24
chapters.text: I asked why God had permitted the deceiver to have such power. The voice answered that human beings were given will: they may desire righteousness or turn toward what God hates. Azazel's will is in lawlessness, but Adam and his descendants are judged for the choices of their own hearts.

chapters.label: Chapter 25
chapters.text: Then I saw violence and murder spreading through generations. I saw impurity, theft, jealousy, and idols. I saw people sacrificing their children and committing abominations. I said, ‘Why have you allowed such evil?’ The voice answered that judgment is delayed until the appointed measure is complete.

chapters.label: Chapter 26
chapters.text: I saw a building like a great temple, and within it priests and sacrifices. Then people of violence entered it, seized its holy things, and burned it with fire. I cried out because of what I saw. God said that this was the sanctuary built in his name, but Israel would provoke him through idolatry and injustice, and enemies would destroy the house.

chapters.label: Chapter 27
chapters.text: I asked how long the destruction would last. The voice spoke of a fixed number of times, divided according to the course of history, until the age of wickedness reached its end. During those times Israel would be chastened among the nations.

chapters.label: Chapter 28
chapters.text: I saw one coming from the left side of the nations, worshiped by many, while some of my people mocked and struck him. I asked who he was. The answer spoke mysteriously of a man set apart to reprove the nations and of the testing that would come upon Israel. The received text here is difficult, and its Christian-looking features may reflect later transmission.

chapters.label: Chapter 29
chapters.text: I saw twelve periods of the age, and within them plagues, famine, fire, sword, and confusion. The Eternal said that these were judgments upon the nations and upon those of Israel who joined themselves to lawlessness. After them the righteous would be gathered.

chapters.label: Chapter 30
chapters.text: The voice named ten plagues of the final age: distress through sickness and need; burning of cities; destruction by wild beasts; famine; earthquake and sword; hail and frost; wild creatures; pestilence and hunger; execution by sword and flight; and thunder, earthquake, and fire. These would humble the world before the final judgment.

chapters.label: Chapter 31
chapters.text: Then a chosen one would come, and God would gather his people from among the nations. Those who had mocked and oppressed them would be judged. The righteous would rejoice, while the rule of Azazel would be ended and the adversary given over to the fire prepared for him.

chapters.label: Chapter 32
chapters.text: The voice said that after the appointed days the trumpet would sound, and God's chosen people would be gathered. The age of corruption would pass away. Abraham was told to return to the earth and keep what had been revealed until the proper time. I came down from the mountain, carrying in my heart the words of the Eternal One and the knowledge of the judgment to come.
